Hi Maya — great questions and thanks for the RFP. Short answer: both routes are viable; the right path depends on timeline and required contract/customization. Quick summary below, then I can lay out concrete next steps.

Marketplace (AWS Private Offer)
- Pros: fastest procurement path for pilots (buyer accepts private offer; marketplace handles billing/invoicing). Good for pilots where you want to start quickly.
- Cons: invoice routing goes through AWS marketplace billing entity (buyer PO must match marketplace invoice). Some enterprise procurement teams prefer direct vendor invoices for internal chargeback.
- Compliance: Redwood will provide SOC2 reports and we can supply audit logs; we simply provide the evidence — billing records live with AWS marketplace for that invoice.
- Co-sell: marketplace purchases are eligible for co-sell but partner credit timelines depend on marketplace reporting windows.

Direct Contract (MSA + Redwood invoice)
- Pros: straight vendor invoicing to your billing entity, direct SLA/terms negotiation, easier for multi-year committed pricing and custom data terms.
- Cons: takes longer for legal/PO setup vs marketplace private offer.

Recommendation: for FinWave (regulated fintech) — if you want to start the pilot quickly, use a Private Offer and we will ensure SOC2 + audit artifacts are provided immediately. For production rollouts and crediting/contractual guarantees, we recommend transitioning to a direct MSA and vendor invoice once procurement/legal can prioritize it.

Next steps I suggest: 1) quick 30-min call with procurement + finance to confirm PO routing needs; 2) Redwood will prepare a Marketplace Private Offer template OR a draft MSA based on which you prefer; 3) Karthik and Laura will confirm co-sell handling and finance implications.

Attaching a short one-pager that explains the billing flow for both options.

— Sean

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Sean — TL;DR: Pilot on Marketplace, production on Direct is the pragmatic path for FinWave. Details: 

- Co-sell / credits: Marketplace purchases can be co-sell eligible, but partner credit (AWS channel incentives) are reconciled on their schedule — often monthly or quarterly depending on reporting. For pipeline attribution and faster co-sell recognition, we should register the opportunity in the AWS Channel Marketplace and tag the private offer with our partner ID; that speeds crediting but doesn't eliminate reconciliation delays.
- Invoicing/PO: If FinWave needs vendor-level invoices for internal chargeback, direct MSA is cleaner. For Marketplace pilots, the invoice will be issued by AWS (marketplace billing) and will reference the Private Offer. We can provide a Redwood-originated order confirmation (non-invoice) to help their finance team reconcile, but it is not a tax invoice in the marketplace flow.
- Compliance/audit artifacts: We can provide SOC2 report, penetration test summary, and S3 access to audit logs (if on a private deployment). For hosted Redwood on marketplace, we still deliver the compliance artifacts; log storage/billing records tied to purchase live in AWS. If FinWave requires specific retention/agreement we should capture that in an MSA addendum (direct contract).
- Timing: Marketplace Private Offer -> typically 3–10 business days from buyer acceptance to first invoice, depending on buyer PO processing. Direct contract (MSA + PO) -> usually 2–6 weeks (legal review).

Recommended operational path for a regulated fintech pilot: 1) Create an AWS Private Offer for the pilot (short term) so engineering can start; 2) Simultaneously start MSA review with our legal team with a target to convert to direct vendor billing before production. This gives FinWave speed without locking them into marketplace-only constraints.

Attaching the Private Offer steps doc for the finops/procurement team to follow.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
